findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments does not exist, so the services module won't compile
findings.body:
`UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), and a repository-wide search finds no no-arg overload. That is a compile error in `services`.

Suggested fix: pass the user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. That fix also needs the predicate problem on UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 sorted out first.

findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI now only shows when a user is already identified, so normal first-time login loses it
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `... && user != null`. Before this change, both call sites filled the WebAuthn form only when the user was *not* yet known:
- the old `authenticate` filled it in the `else` branch (user == null);
- the old `challenge` checked `context.getUser() == null && ...`.

Now `authenticate` (line 115) and `challenge` (line 137) call `fillContextForm` only when `context.getUser() != null`. So on an ordinary login where no user is set yet:
- `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` and the challenge are never set, and the passkey option is gone from the username/password page.
- After an invalid-user error (`testInvalidUser` → `challenge`, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:105-111) the passkeys stay hidden as well.

This breaks tests this PR keeps or adds. For example, `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` asserts `//form[@id='webauth']` on a fresh login (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:146), and so do the new tests at lines 196 and 238.

The re-authentication fix needs passkeys in *both* cases. Suggested predicate: `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, plus whatever per-user restriction is intended when `user != null`.

findings.title: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` turns passkeys off for the realm, so it never tests a user without a passkey
findings.body:
The comment at line 304 says passkeys should not be offered "as this user does not have passkey". But the test sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so passkeys are hidden for every user because of the realm setting.

The case that matters for this change is not covered: passkeys enabled in the realm, and a re-authenticating user who has only a password. It is also the case most affected by the new `user != null` logic, and by `UsernameForm` no longer skipping the form during re-authentication.

Suggestion: add a variant with passkeys enabled for `test-user@localhost`, or reword the comment.

findings.title: The `try { assertThat(..., nullValue()); fail(); } catch (Exception)` absence check is convoluted
findings.body:
`findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is absent, so `assertThat(..., nullValue())` can never pass. The check works only because `fail()` throws an `AssertionError`, which `catch (Exception)` does not catch.

The Organization test in this same PR uses a clearer form: `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))`. It would read better here (lines 291-296 and 312-317), and catching `Exception` broadly could also hide unrelated failures.

findings.title: Add `@Override` to `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`
findings.body: This method overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128). Without `@Override`, a later rename or signature change in the parent would silently stop the override from applying.

contracts.action: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate/challenge fill WebAuthn conditional-UI data based on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code filled the form only when context.getUser() == null (else branch / challenge guard)
contracts.before_after: Before: passkeys data shown when no user was identified, and never shown for re-authentication. After: shown only when the user is identified, so a fresh login no longer gets it.
contracts.visible_effect: The webauth form / passkey autocomplete disappears from the normal login page and after invalid-username errors.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent regression: passkey login is no longer offered on first-time login.

contracts.action: UsernameForm no longer skips the form for an already-set user when passkeys are enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate for user != null (hidden username, registration disabled, USER_SET_BEFORE note)
contracts.before_after: Calls a non-existent no-arg overload, so the code does not compile.

contracts.equivalent_path: AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler, which calls the same helper (formerly inlined)
contracts.before_after: Both paths set USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED when the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note is true, then render the challenge.

summary:
The PR says it fixes re-authentication with passkeys, but as it stands it doesn't compile and it breaks passkey login on a normal first-time login.

**Blockers**
- **Compile error:** `UsernameForm.java:47` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only version takes a `UserModel` (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`), and there is no no-argument overload anywhere in the repository.
- **Condition is inverted:** the new check (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:161`) requires `user != null`. Passkeys are now offered only during re-authentication and no longer on a normal login. Before, they were shown exactly when no user was known yet. Tests this PR keeps or adds expect the passkey form on a fresh login (`PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:146`, `:196` and `:238`), so they would fail.

**Smaller points (author's call)**
- **Missing test case:** `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` turns passkeys off for the whole realm. It never covers a user without a passkey in a realm where passkeys are on, which is the case this change affects most.
- **Awkward absence check:** the tests confirm the passkey form is missing with a convoluted try/fail/catch. `Assert.assertThrows`, already used in the Organization test, is clearer.
- **Missing `@Override`:** `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` should have it.

The rest of the change looks fine:
- The new shared helper `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` does the same thing as the code it replaced, and the passkey error path now reuses it.
- A passkey belonging to a different user is still rejected during re-authentication by the existing user-mismatch check in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.action`.

I only read the code; nothing was built or run.
